newsitem.title: UK: UK to resist longer Eurotunnel concession -paper.
newsitem.headline: UK to resist longer Eurotunnel concession -paper.

text.p: Any demand for an extension of the concession of Anglo-French Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel will be resisted by the UK government, the Times newspaper said in its Wednesday edition.

Earlier on Tuesday sources close to talks on restructuring Eurotunnel's debt mountain said the company reached an outline agreement with six of its bank lenders. The company has been seeking an agreement on the pricing of an expected debt-for- equity swap and the issue of convertible bonds, which would lighten Eurotunnel's debt burden.
Eurotunnel operates the rail tunnel that was opened in 1994. It froze payments to 225 banks on junior-ranked debt in September 1995 and set about negotiating new terms.

But the company only has a limited 65-year concession to operate the tunnel and the Times said a demand to the French and British governments for an extension of this is believed to be part of the rescue plan agreed with the banks.

The paper said that, while the UK government faces pressure from ferry operators not to "subsidise" Eurotunnel, which has had a sharp impact on the ferry companies' profits, it is likely to give way if the alternative was insolvency for Eurotunnel. Eurotunnel's shares were suspended on Monday in anticipation of the outcome of the talks being announced.
